title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: November 13 | Week 10 vs. Los Angeles Rams
headline: A rookie third-string QB (Carson) makes his first start vs. the Rams, with Hayden Conner moving to center; Trey McBride was named captain and Josh Sweat looks fine.
summary: LaFleur opened with the injury report. Gaines and, I believe, Froholdt are out, and Zack Carter (not on the roster, so unclear) was also mentioned as out. Everyone else is either good or questionable. Roy Lopez has a chance to play and will be judged day by day, Bam Knight has no designation, and Darius Robinson has something new from Wednesday's practice that will be clearer through Sunday. Josh Sweat missed Thursday's practice but LaFleur said he feels good. Hayden Conner slides from guard to center, and the main challenge is making and owning the line calls. McBride was named a captain, which LaFleur linked to his daily work ethic and his authenticity, and said the vote was close in the preseason. With Jacoby Brissett gone, the offense will be run by the rookie QB Carson. LaFleur praised his intelligence, said the wristband play calls will be phased out gradually rather than all at once, and expects good and bad plays in his first start. He also praised Zay Jones's work in the offense and his veteran experience.

title: Joe Brady Talks About Amani Hooker's Week Of Practice
headline: Bills RT Spencer Brown is not ruled out and will be evaluated Saturday, so swing tackle Tylan Grable could start on the right side again. Newly traded safety Amani Hooker is 'definitely going to play'.

Brady was very impressed with how fast the newly acquired safety (Amani Hooker, per the video title) is picking up the scheme and language. title: Dave Canales previews Panthers at Saints matchup

He also said Jaelan Phillips had a great week, feels confident and is excited to return, with little scheme change for the outside linebackers. Several players are questionable, and decisions will come after Friday-afternoon talks with the coaches before the report is announced. Canales also said the offense found its explosive plays again through a growing run game and better protection choices, and he expressed trust in the kicker despite a recent miss.

headline: Lions are healthy heading into Munich: Amon-Ra St. Brown is the emotional focus, and the only injury mentioned was a minor chest issue for a player whose name the captions garbled (apparently an offensive blocker). Campbell says the offense will stay aggressive, including on fourth down.

He credited the defense, under coordinator Kelvin Sheppard, with cleaning up details and playing complementary football for about four weeks. He described his aggressive nature on fourth downs, citing faith in Goff, St. Brown, Gibbs, LaPorta, Jameson Williams and the offensive line, while noting game context matters. title: Matt LaFleur previews rivalry matchup vs. Vikings
headline: Chris Brooks' status is still undecided and Tucker Kraft is not a lock for Sunday. LaFleur expects a tough, low-scoring game against a Vikings defense he called possibly the NFL's best.
summary: LaFleur spent most of the session on the Vikings defense. He praised its coordination, its aggressive pressure packages, and the ball skills of its whole secondary. He called it one of the top-ranked defenses, possibly the best, in the league. He said it is especially tough in the red zone and at putting offenses behind the sticks, so the Packers have to stay on schedule. Asked whether he would lean on the ground game as he did last year, he said "potentially" and that it depends on how the game unfolds. On health, Chris Brooks' status will be decided after Friday's practice, and LaFleur noted his main value is as a returner. Tucker Kraft looks good in practice but has few reps, so the team wants to keep building him up and will decide after Friday. title: Coach John Harbaugh reviews Giants vs. Commanders
headline: Harbaugh says the Giants came out of the Thursday loss to Washington healthy, with a returning player due back next week. He is more confident in J.J. McCarthy than ever and defended Malik Nabers on the last play. Jacksonville is next.
summary: Harbaugh reviewed the loss to Washington, saying the end-of-game run calls after the two interceptions were meant to burn clock and timeouts, though a pass might have been better. He said he is more confident than ever in McCarthy, who is in his third or fourth start, and he defended the late deep throws against zero blitzes as split-second quarterback decisions rather than mismanagement. He said Nabers was trying to track the ball on the final play and did nothing willful, and he denied that Cam Skattebo's earlier fumble against Washington affected the late-game play calling. He said the offensive line played well and ran the ball much better than against the Eagles, and he is looking for more consistency. He acknowledged a technique problem with the kicker's plant foot on right-hash kicks. He called the fourth-down punts in the 50s coin-flip decisions and said he may be more aggressive in future. He also said the "who let the dogs out" cadence was an attempt to draw Washington offside that he would not repeat. The team has a long break, came out healthy, and expects to get a player back next week before it turns to Jacksonville.

injuries.detail: Harbaugh said the team should get him back next week; the name does not match anyone on the roster, so the identity is unverified. He added that the team came out of the game healthy with nothing lingering.

signals.claim: McCarthy remains the starting QB and the team will grow its confidence in having him close out games.
signals.note: The coach is publicly backing McCarthy as a capable starter, so his job looks secure and late-game passing trust should grow.
signals.quote: I think he's proven that he's capable of winning games and making the plays.

signals.note: Nabers was open on a deep seam on the final drive, and the coach defended him on the last play, so his target share is unlikely to be affected.
signals.quote: I don't think there's anything willful about not doing it, that's for sure.

signals.quote: No.

Harbaugh said kicker Dominic Zavada has a plant-foot technique issue on the right hash that needs cleaning up. The punts in the 50s were toss-up decisions leaning toward punting, partly because of wind and field position, and he may be more aggressive on fourth down in future.
The play involving Skattebo was a normal quarterback sneak with a check, not the tush push, so he wasn't supposed to be pushing. The team has 4 or 5 different sneak and push calls.
With extra rest the team gets a short break and returns Tuesday. Harbaugh said the team played fast on a short week. He plays down the tough upcoming schedule, saying they expect to win every game.
The "who let the dogs out" cadence was an attempt to draw Washington offside. Harbaugh said he wouldn't try it again and that he probably should have gone for it on fourth down instead.

title: Postgame Press Conference: Coach John Harbaugh on loss to Commanders
headline: Cam Skattebo (two TDs) and Isaiah Likely impressed in the loss, J.J. McCarthy earned strong praise, and Harbaugh is sticking with his rookie kicker.
summary: Harbaugh called the Thursday night loss to Washington disappointing but said his team's spirit is fine and the division goals haven't changed. He said the Giants played a good game that fell short, citing a critical false start, plays left unfinished, some leaky tackling, and runs that gave up a bit too much. He explained that the final throws came against zero blitzes. He had considered going for it on a fourth down but would only have done so at four yards or less, and he tried to draw Washington offsides on the last fourth down. He was strongly positive on J.J. McCarthy, praising his legs and his throws, including a touchdown pass to Isaiah Likely that he called one of the best plays of the season. He said Cam Skattebo played really well, with two touchdowns, and that the offensive line looked more like it did against Houston. On the rookie kicker's latest miss, he said he won't panic or knee-jerk, believes in him, and will keep giving him chances. He attributed the lack of pressure on the Commanders' quarterback to his mobility and a lot of play action on early downs. He said seven tough games remain and the team needs to win enough to take the division. He declined to explain specific short-yardage sneak and crack sweep failures until he sees the tape.

signals.claim: McCarthy remains the starting QB and is developing, with a career-high in passing yards in this game.

signals.quote: I thought JJ played very well.

signals.note: He scored twice and drew praise, which supports his volume and touchdown potential.

topics.detail: After another missed kick, Harbaugh said he has confidence in his rookie kicker, won't make a knee-jerk change at the midpoint of the season, and said it's up to the kicker to make his kicks.

Harbaugh said the offensive line played much better, more like it did at Houston, and the run game was good. He also said Washington stopped the late third-down run and a quarterback sneak, but he wanted to see the tape before commenting.
The Giants struggled to pressure Washington's quarterback because he moves well and the Commanders used lots of play action and stayed out of third-and-long.

The final throws came against zero blitzes. Harbaugh considered going for a fourth down but said he'd have done it only at four yards or less, and he tried to draw Washington offsides on the last fourth down. He defended a quarterback crack sweep from an empty backfield as having an extra blocker.

Harbaugh called the loss a missed chance to separate in the division but said the goals haven't changed. He expects seven tough games ahead and said the team has to win enough of them to take the division.

He said Geno Smith was visibly upset after the Kansas City loss, and he wants that frustration channeled into the Bills game. headline: Commanders escaped with a late win after Jayden Daniels threw back-to-back interceptions and still led the game-winning drive. Stefon Diggs was singled out for his end-of-half and end-of-game plays.
summary: Quinn opened by saying the team needed this win and that he sensed it would come down to the end. He pointed to close finishes in 2024 and 2025 and said it would have been easy to lose faith after a fourth-down stop, a big touchdown allowed, and then back-to-back interceptions thrown by Jayden Daniels. He praised Daniels for shaking off the picks, which he said hadn't happened in a long time, and for leading both a two-minute drive before halftime and the final drive. Stefon Diggs came up in connection with the end of the half and the final scoring drive. Quinn also gave credit to Luke McCaffrey for a smart play that won't appear in the box score. Defensively, he liked the aggressive blitz-heavy approach at the end, said the unit's confidence and communication are trending up, and praised the pairing of Frankie Luvu and Sonny Styles. He explained his successful challenge as a gamble he was happy to take, since he would likely have called a timeout there anyway. He called it the most adversity and the most belief he has seen from the team, and said there is still plenty to clean up.
